status.label: Inactive
status.shortComment: The Panthers are hopeful that Coker (quadriceps) will be ready to return to action following their Week 5 bye, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
status.longComment: After making an early exit from the Panthers' Week 3 loss to the Browns due to a quad strain, Coker missed one practice and was limited in two others before taking a questionable tag into this past Sunday's game against the Lions. He was ultimately inactive for the Panthers' 32-26 win, but the team is optimistic that with another week off to heal up from the injury, Coker will be ready to go for a Week 6 matchup with the Eagles on Oct. 18. Despite essentially playing just two and a half games this season, Coker has been highly productive during his time on the field with an 18-222-2 receiving line on 22 targets.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: The Panthers placed Legette (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
status.longComment: Legette has been working through a knee injury the last two weeks, and while he was slated to miss a second straight contest Sunday against the Lions, he'll now sit out at least the next four (including Week 4), meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 8 versus the Broncos. In Legette's continued absence, Carolina will lean on Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker (quadriceps), Brycen Tremayne, John Metchie and David Moore at wide receiver.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Freeling (knee) could return to the field as soon as the Panthers' Week 6 game against the Eagles on Sunday, Oct. 18, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported Monday.
status.longComment: Freeling suffered a knee injury in the third quarter of the Panthers' Week 4 win over the Lions. With the Week 5 bye buying Freeling some valuable recovery time, it's possible he's able to get healthy enough to suit up against Philadelphia. If Freeling ultimately misses any time, Stone Forsythe will likely start at right tackle.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Phillips (hamstring) could return to the Panthers' lineup as early as the Week 6 game against the Eagles on Sunday, Oct. 18, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported Monday.
status.longComment: Phillips sustained a hamstring injury in the Panthers' Week 4 win over the Lions. The linebacker is week-to-week with the injury and has the benefit of Carolina's Week 5 bye to aid in the recovery process. Princely Umanmielen or Trevis Gipson would likely start at strong-side linebacker opposite Patrick Jones if Phillips ultimately can't make it back in time for the Week 6 matchup against Philadelphia.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: Head coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that Jackson (groin) underwent core-muscle surgery and will be sidelined about eight weeks, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
status.longComment: The Panthers are in a code-red situation at cornerback after both starters, Jackson and Jaycee Horn (quadriceps), suffered significant injuries against Cleveland in Week 3. Ahead of a date with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams on national television Sunday night, Carolina will be relying on Will Lee, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade to cover the snaps.
